jobs.description:
Purpose Statement/Position Summary:

The Security Executive Director has strategic oversight of CHLA Security. Manages, supervises, plans, and directs the hospital's security program and security personnel. Develops, implements, and enforces security strategies, policies, procedures, and standards to ensure the safety and security of patients, visitors, staff, property, assets, and organizational information. Maintains compliance with applicable security regulations, standards, and organizational policies. Conducts security assessments, inspections, and monitoring activities, including oversight of physical security technologies and digital risk monitoring programs. Oversee efforts to identify, assess, and mitigate online threats, publicly exposed information, and reputational risks through ongoing monitoring, threat intelligence, information suppression, and remediation activities. Develops and delivers security-related training and communications to ensure staff are informed of security policies, procedures, and potential risks. Establishes and maintains operational plans for emergency response, disaster recovery, evacuation, workplace violence prevention and response, and other security-related incidents. Coordinates with local, state, and federal agencies, as well as external security partners, to remain current on security threats, directives, regulations, and best practices. Develop and implement protocols that promote a secure environment for patients, staff, and visitors.

Required:

Minimum Qualifications/Work Experience:

8+ years of progressive experience in physical security, security operations, workplace violence prevention, threat assessment and management, investigations, emergency preparedness, security technology, and law enforcement coordination, with demonstrated success in conducting security risk assessments; developing security strategies, policies, budgets, staffing models, and performance metrics; and exercising strong leadership, communication, problem-solving, change management, and discretion in handling sensitive and confidential matters.

Preferred:

Extensive knowledge of healthcare security operations, including the protection of patients, visitors, staff, physicians, facilities, and critical infrastructure, with demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with clinical and administrative leaders, Human Resources, Legal, Risk Management, Marketing and Communications, Information Technology, and law enforcement, as well as strong knowledge of healthcare accreditation standards and applicable federal, state, and local regulatory requirements related to hospital security and workplace safety.

Education/Licensure/Certification:

Required:

Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and substantial relevant professional experience.
Demonstrated knowledge of the Hospital Incident Command System (HICS), National Incident Management System (NIMS), and Incident Command System (ICS), including experience supporting hospital emergency operations, incident command and coordination with law enforcement, fire, EMS and other public safety partners.

Preferred:

Advanced degree in security management, criminal justice, business administration, healthcare administration, emergency management or related discipline.
One or more of the following: Certified Protection Professional (CPP), Physical Security Professional (PSP), Certified Healthcare Protection Administrator (CHPA), and/or Certified Threat Manager (CTM).
Prior law enforcement, military, government security or other relevant public safety experience combined with substantial healthcare security leadership experience.

jobs.description:
About Evolve Treatment Centers:

Evolve offers the best in therapy and recovery options for residential and outpatient treatment programs for teens. We help adolescents 12 to 17 years old struggling with mental health, substance abuse, or behavior issues. Evolve offers a one-of-a-kind experience that serves teens and their families from across the country from our California-based treatment centers. We focus on positivity, equipping teens for change, and growing the whole person in a setting that’s comfortable and feels like home.

Job Summary:

The Clinical Director is an experienced, licensed clinician who oversees the clinical operations of two Evolve residential programs located in La Mesa, CA. The Clinical Director works alongside the Operations Manager to ensure that all administrative, operations, and compliance needs are being met. All duties listed below apply to both programs that the Clinical Director oversees.

Clinical Responsibilities:

Provide clinical oversight to the programs and ensure that all quality, clinical excellence, and safety measures are maintained.
Provide clinical supervision to unlicensed staff per BBS requirements
Provide tours for prospective clients and their families and support Primary Therapists as needed in supporting client’s families
Ensure that the program’s clinical approach remains behavioral and skills-based and in line with Evolve’s mission and values.
Facilitate weekly Treatment Team meetings, regular clinical trainings and provide clinical mentorship, compile behavioral feedback for clients, and ensure meeting notes are taken and distributed
Regularly review and audit clinical documentation for the program in order to maintain internal and licensing standards
Assist with coverage of individual, family, and group therapy sessions as needed during Primary Therapist absences.

Managerial Responsibilities:

Provide leadership, mentorship, and guidance to the teams
Provide direct supervision and facilitate weekly meetings with the Primary Therapists, and Operations Manager to provide oversight and individualized support.
Evaluate the performance and competence of staff, and when necessary, discipline and discharge subordinate staff in accordance with established personnel policies (i.e.: Performance evaluations, Coaching Plans, etc.)
Collaborate with the Operations Manager to oversee Residential Counselor and Chef performance and participate in implementation of performance reviews and disciplinary action.
Create and maintain a positive, collaborative team culture and collaborate with the Operations Manager to facilitate quarterly team-building activities for the team.
Provide staff with updates/ changes to policies, procedures, and organizational goals
Maintain the program schedule and ensure that it adheres to Evolve’s program schedule requirements

Qualifications:

Licensed for at least 2 years in California as a LMFT/LCSW/LPCC
Must be able to pass a Live Scan background check
Exceptional clinical judgment
Knowledge and experience in various therapeutic orientations and treatment modalities
Provides clear communication both in person and via email
Demonstrates sensitivity and attentiveness to clinical needs related to disability and/or racial, ethnic, cultural, sexual and gender identity
Knowledge of adolescent mental health and co-occurring disorders
Ability to work in a fast-paced, challenging, and dynamic environment
Excellent interpersonal skills and the ability to maintain a positive collaborative relationship among staff

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience working with adolescents, particularly those with mental health and substance abuse issues
Experience with supervision and management

$120,000 - $135,000

jobs.title: Program Director, Practice Management Consultant
jobs.description:
SEI's Wealth business is seeking a results-oriented Practice Management Consultant
to specialize in helping advisory firms gain and maintain scale—capacity, efficiency, and consistency—through their people and culture.

This people-centric leader will be responsible for helping to build and evolve SEI's Practice Management "scale" function in close partnership with SEI’s Technology and Operations Consultant and alongside the "growth" and "evolve" functions. An ideal candidate is willing and able to strategize, experiment, and execute solutions that deliver actionable and impactful advice and resources to SEI’s independent broker dealer and RIA clients. We're looking for an individual who is an expert in all things talent—hiring, onboarding, management, leadership, culture, talent development, and compensation planning—helping firms build and develop high-performing teams that drive sustainable growth, profitability, and enterprise value.

This role will also help advisory firms evolve their talent strategy to evolve in an everchanging, digital and AI-native world—reimagining roles, workflows, competencies, and career paths as AI and automation reshape how advisory work gets done. The consultant will guide firms in identifying which capabilities to build internally, which to augment with technology, and how to prepare their teams to thrive alongside AI-enabled tools and platforms.

Equally important, this consultant will help advisors think like business owners when it comes to their people—treating talent and productivity as strategic investments rather than operational expenses. They will coach firm leaders on measuring return on talent, aligning compensation and productivity, making disciplined hiring and workforce planning decisions, and building the systems, metrics, and management practices that turn a group of professionals into a scalable, high-performing enterprise.

This practice management role is tailored for individuals deeply enthusiastic about the independent advisor profession, committed to ongoing learning, and able to leverage their expertise in talent, people, and culture to drive meaningful outcomes within advisory practices. An ideal candidate possesses a background as a Chief People Officer, Head of Talent, HR leader, COO, business owner, coach, or consultant with substantial real-world experience helping service businesses build and scale high-performing teams, and is experienced and networked in the wealth management industry. They understand the unique talent challenges of independent advisory firms of all sizes—both small ($100M+) and large firms ($2B+ AUM)—and are excited to expand our practice management advice and resources to support scalable growth through people.

This role is a remote role. The role requires up to 20% travel.

What You Will Do

Provide expert consultation, coaching, and education to independent advisory practices on talent-focused practice management topics, including hiring, onboarding, performance management, leadership development, organizational design, compensation planning, employee engagement, retention, and culture building.
Help advisory firms evolve their talent strategy for a digital and AI-native world—guiding them to redesign roles, workflows, competencies, and career paths so their teams can thrive alongside AI and automation.
Coach advisors to think like business owners when it comes to their people—treating talent and productivity as strategic investments, measuring return on talent, and applying disciplined workforce planning, capacity, and compensation decisions to drive profitability and enterprise value.
Be an integral, expert resource to help SEI attract and onboard mid-to-large and growing advisory firms ($500M+) by demonstrating how strong talent strategies drive business results.
Conduct thorough assessments of firms' talent, leadership, organizational, and cultural strengths, gaps, and readiness, and offer actionable and customized recommendations.
Develop and deliver engaging content including presentations, workshops, and training sessions to advisors and their teams on talent, people, culture, and related practice management topics.
Create scalable resources, tools, playbooks, frameworks, and educational content to help advisors plan for and execute team-building, leadership succession, and culture development as they grow organically and inorganically.
Build and deliver curriculum designed to develop the next generation of advisors, operations leads, and firm leaders—supporting career pathing, competency building, and long-term firm sustainability.
Lead and grow the SEI Next Gen Community, creating meaningful development experiences, peer networking opportunities, and ongoing educational programming for emerging advisor and operations talent.
Partner closely with SEI's People and Culture team to bring proven talent best practices to SEI's advisor clients, including StrengthsFinder, DISC, and other behavioral assessments, leadership development tools, and organizational effectiveness frameworks.
Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to advance how SEI connects talent with hiring advisory firms at scale.
Work in close partnership with fellow Practice Management Consultants across the growth, scale, and transition pillars to deliver holistic, integrated advice to advisors.
Build and manage strategic partnerships with external talent-focused experts, consultants, coaches, assessment providers, and service providers to deliver additional value to advisors.
Direct and manage special projects on the Advisor Services Team related to talent, workforce development, and culture-focused strategies.
Act as a thought leader by contributing articles, webinars, podcasts, and other educational content on talent, leadership, and culture within advisory firms.

What We Need From You

A minimum of 7 years of experience helping financial advisors and/or professional service firms grow, scale, and strengthen their businesses through roles in talent management, human resources, organizational development, coaching, consulting, practice management, or leadership within advisory firms.
Deep expertise across the full employee lifecycle, including workforce planning, recruiting, onboarding, performance management, leadership development, compensation design, succession planning, engagement, and retention.
Working knowledge of how AI, automation, and digital tools are reshaping roles, workflows, and productivity within professional service and advisory firms—and how to translate that into practical talent strategy.
Business-owner mindset with the ability to help firm leaders view talent and productivity as strategic investments—measuring ROI, aligning compensation with outcomes, and connecting people decisions to enterprise value.
First-hand experience building, leading, and developing high-performing teams—ideally within advisory firms or similar professional service businesses.
Deep understanding of the independent advisor and RIA landscape, including the unique talent, leadership, and culture challenges facing advisory firms today.
Experience designing and facilitating leadership development programs, team workshops, and educational experiences for professionals at all career stages.
Exceptional communication skills, both written and verbal, with an ability to present complex topics in a clear, confident, and compelling way.
Experience in multi-channel communication mediums, including individual face-to-face interactions, in-person and virtual one-to-many presentations, live video, recorded video, phone and email.
Proven track record of driving successful team-building, leadership effectiveness, engagement, retention, and cultural outcomes for organizations and their staff.
Strategic thinker with the ability to translate high-level talent strategies into practical, actionable advice and plans.
Passion for developing others, particularly next-generation advisor and operations talent.
Highly collaborative, entrepreneurial, and growth minded.
Willingness to travel up to 25% of the time to support advisor events, presentations, community programming, and relationship management efforts.

What We Would Like From You

Professional certifications such as SHRM-CP, SHRM-SCP, SPHR, Gallup Certified Strengths Coach, DISC Certification, ICF Coaching credentials, CFP®, CIMA®, or CEPA® are advantageous but not mandatory.
Experience designing educational content, curriculum, playbooks, or decision frameworks to support advisor team-building and leadership development.
Experience helping firms adopt AI-enabled tools, redesign workflows, or build digital-first operating models.
Experience building and leading peer communities, mentorship programs, or leadership academies.
Familiarity with compensation benchmarking, career pathing frameworks, productivity metrics, and organizational design for advisory firms.
Proficiency in analyzing people metrics, productivity data, and organizational performance data to inform talent strategies and investment decisions.
Someone who will embody our SEI Values of courage, integrity, collaboration, inclusion, connection and fun. Please see our website for more information. https://www.seic.com/

Citi Commercial Bank (CCB)
San Francisco, California

About Citi Commercial Bank

Citi Commercial Bank ("CCB") is part of Citi, a leading global financial services company serving clients in over 180 countries. Citi's vision is to be the preeminent banking partner for institutions with cross-border needs, a global leader in wealth management and a valued personal bank in our home market of the United States.

CCB is the bank of choice for growth-oriented, mid-sized companies looking to scale rapidly and expand internationally. Leveraging Citi's global network, comprehensive product capabilities, and industry expertise, we help innovative companies navigate complexity, accelerate growth, and achieve their strategic ambitions. Our clients value Citi as a trusted advisor that delivers strategic insights, global connectivity, and tailored financial solutions.

Description

Citi Commercial Bank is seeking a Managing Director, Technology Banker based in San Francisco to further strengthen our Technology banking franchise and accelerate growth across the innovation economy.

The successful candidate will serve as a senior coverage banker responsible for originating, developing, and deepening relationships with high-growth technology companies across the San Francisco Bay Area and broader technology ecosystem. The role will play a critical part in expanding CCB's market presence, increasing connectivity with venture capital investors, founders, management teams, and industry influencers, while delivering the full capabilities of Citi to clients.

This position requires a highly respected technology banker with deep market expertise, established credibility within the technology sector, and a proven ability to originate business opportunities and build enduring client relationships. The individual will work closely with partners across Commercial Banking, Corporate Banking, Investment Banking, Treasury & Trade Solutions, Markets, Wealth, and other Citi businesses to deliver integrated solutions and drive franchise growth.

The role is intended to enhance Citi's presence within the Technology ecosystem and support the continued expansion of CCB's technology franchise, while aligning closely with Citi's broader Banking growth strategy in the San Francisco Bay Area.

The Managing Director, Technology Banker will report to the North America CCB Digital, Technology and Communications (DT&C) head.

Key Responsibilities

Strategy & Franchise Development

Support execution of CCB's technology growth strategy by increasing market penetration and expanding Citi's presence across target technology client segments.
Identify emerging trends, disruptive technologies, and evolving business models across the technology sector.
Provide market intelligence and strategic insights to senior leadership regarding opportunities, risks, and competitive dynamics.
Serve as a visible ambassador for Citi within the San Francisco technology ecosystem and contribute to strengthening the firm's industry profile.

Client Coverage & Business Development

Develop and execute a client coverage strategy focused on growth-stage and VC-backed technology companies throughout the San Francisco Bay Area.
Originate new client relationships and expand existing relationships by delivering the full breadth of Citi's banking capabilities and fostering deep engagement across the firm's product and advisory platforms.
Build trusted advisor relationships with founders, CEOs, CFOs, boards, private equity sponsors, venture investors, and senior executives across the technology sector.
Drive wallet growth through proactive identification of client needs and delivery of tailored banking solutions.
Partner with product specialists and banking colleagues to provide strategic advice and innovative financial solutions throughout the client lifecycle.
Identify and pursue opportunities within emerging technology subsectors and evolving business models.

Technology Ecosystem Leadership

Develop and maintain strong relationships with venture capital firms, private equity sponsors, startup founders, accelerators, incubators, and other key participants within the innovation economy.
Expand Citi's connectivity across the technology ecosystem to enhance market intelligence, client acquisition, and franchise development.
Represent Citi at industry conferences, forums, networking events, and thought leadership opportunities.
Drive industry thought leadership internally and externally through market insights, client events, and strategic engagement initiatives.
Maintain deep knowledge of competitive positioning, capital flows, emerging technologies, and sector developments.

One Citi Partnership

Collaborate closely with partners across Commercial Banking, Corporate Banking, Investment Banking, Treasury & Trade Solutions, Markets, Wealth, and other Citi businesses to deliver a coordinated "One Citi" approach.
Drive innovation through the development and delivery of industry-specific solutions in partnership with product specialists and subject matter experts.
Identify opportunities to bring the full breadth of Citi's capabilities to technology clients across their growth journey.
Help deepen connectivity between CCB and Banking teams in support of broader franchise objectives in the Bay Area.

Risk Management

Maintain strong credit and risk discipline while supporting sustainable business growth.
Partner with Risk, Credit, and Underwriting teams to evaluate opportunities and ensure activities are consistent with Citi's risk appetite and policies.
Exercise sound judgment in balancing risk and return objectives while delivering solutions that meet client needs.
Ensure all business activities are conducted in compliance with applicable regulatory requirements, Citi policies, and governance standards.
Appropriately assess risk when business decisions are made, safeguarding Citi, its clients, and its reputation.

Knowledge / Experience

15+ years of commercial banking, corporate banking, technology banking, investment banking, or related financial services experience.
Proven Managing Director-level experience with an established reputation in the technology sector.
Demonstrated success originating, developing, and expanding relationships with high-growth and established technology companies.
Deep understanding of the technology industry, including software, fintech, internet, digital infrastructure, AI, technology-enabled services, and emerging business models.
Strong knowledge of venture capital ecosystems, private equity sponsors, founders, and innovation networks.
Significant experience advising clients on commercial banking, treasury management, lending, capital markets, and strategic financing solutions.
In-depth knowledge of commercial and corporate banking products, including cash management, derivatives, syndicated and bilateral loans, capital markets issuances, trade solutions, and working capital products.
Significant experience with credit decision-making authority, including complex capital structures and cross-border transactions.
Proven ability to collaborate effectively across businesses and deliver integrated client solutions within a matrix organization.
Established network across the San Francisco Bay Area technology and venture capital community.
Strong track record of business development, revenue generation, and franchise expansion.

Skills & Competencies

Recognized industry expert with strong market credibility and executive presence.
Exceptional relationship-building and client management capabilities.
Strong business development orientation with a demonstrated ability to generate new opportunities and expand client relationships.
Highly focused, able to rapidly determine key priorities, clearly communicate those priorities, and effectively marshal resources.
Strong execution skills and results-driven mindset with sound financial acumen.
Strategic thinker with deep commercial judgment and entrepreneurial orientation.
Excellent communication, influencing, presentation, and negotiation skills.
Ability to navigate complex organizations and build productive partnerships across multiple stakeholders.
Strong collaboration skills with a proven ability to foster relationships across teams, products, and businesses.
Ability to adapt quickly to changing market conditions, business priorities, and emerging technologies.
High level of personal integrity and commitment to Citi's values and risk culture.
Ability to work effectively in a matrix environment.

Qualifications

jobs.title: Vice President & Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
Job Description

The Department of Hospital Administration at SUNY Downstate Health Sciences University is seeking a full-time Vice President & Chief Operating Officer.

Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer, the Chief Operating Officer (COO) of SUNY University Hospital at Downstate serves as a key member of the executive leadership team with enterprise-wide responsibility for hospital operations, operational performance, and care delivery systems.

The COO provides strategic and operational leadership across all clinical and support services, with accountability for the hospital’s day-to-day operations, quality and safety outcomes, workforce performance, and overall operational and financial performance in partnership with the Chief Financial Officer. This role ensures the delivery of high-quality, patient-centered care while advancing the hospital’s mission as Brooklyn’s only academic medical center and a critical safety-net provider serving diverse and underserved communities.

SUNY University Hospital at Downstate is a 342-bed academic medical center serving nearly 3 million people across Brooklyn and the surrounding communities, with a critical role as a regional safety-net provider.

Working in close collaboration with the CEO and senior leadership of SUNY Downstate Health Sciences University, the COO plays a central role in executing the organization’s strategic priorities and driving enterprise performance. The COO leads large-scale operational transformation efforts, including improving patient access and throughput, advancing clinical service line performance, and supporting major capital and facility modernization initiatives. This role is instrumental in positioning the hospital for long-term sustainability, operational excellence, and growth in clinical, academic, and community impact.

The COO also partners with executive leadership and governance bodies to ensure alignment with regulatory requirements, institutional priorities, and performance expectations.

Key Responsibilities Operational and Enterprise Leadership Provide executive oversight of all hospital operations, ensuring safe, efficient, and high-quality clinical and support services across the enterprise.

Direct the operational management of inpatient, outpatient, ambulatory, perioperative, and support service functions.

Establish and maintain an effective operating model that aligns operational priorities with the hospital’s mission, strategic plan, and academic objectives.

Ensure operational alignment across clinical departments, administrative functions, and academic programs.

Financial and Operational Performance Share accountability with executive leadership for overall hospital financial performance, including operating margin, cost management, and resource utilization.

Partner closely with the Chief Financial Officer to align operational strategies with financial goals, including revenue optimization and expense management.

Develop and implement performance management systems, including dashboards and key performance indicators, to monitor operational, financial, and quality outcomes.

Drive measurable improvements in efficiency, productivity, and throughput across all areas of the organization.

Performance Improvement and Operational Excellence Lead enterprise-wide initiatives to improve patient access, patient flow, length of stay, throughput, and care coordination.

Foster a culture of continuous improvement through data-driven decisionmaking, operational best practices, and process improvement methodologies.

Benchmark performance against peer academic medical centers and implement best practices to enhance competitiveness and outcomes.

Vice President & Chief Operating Officer Clinical Service Line Strategy and Operations Partner with physician leaders, department chairs, and administrative leadership to optimize clinical service line performance, growth, and market positioning.

Support strategic growth and operational advancement in priority service lines, including cardiology, oncology, perioperative services, and ambulatory care.

Strengthen integration across inpatient, outpatient, and community-based services to improve continuity of care and patient outcomes.

Infrastructure, Capital, and Operational Readiness Collaborate with the CEO and executive leadership to support the implementation of major capital investments and facility modernization initiatives.

Lead operational planning and readiness efforts for new facilities, expanded programs, and clinical services.

Ensure operational alignment with construction, regulatory, and transition timelines for capital projects and hospital expansion efforts.

Workforce and Organizational Leadership Foster a high-performing, engaged workforce aligned with the hospital’s mission, values, and performance expectations.

Partner with Human Resources and clinical leadership on workforce planning, recruitment, retention, and leadership development strategies.

Promote collaboration and alignment among physicians, nurses, and multidisciplinary teams.

Support labor relations strategies and workforce engagement in a complex, unionized healthcare environment.

Quality, Safety, and Regulatory Compliance Support and advance enterprise-wide initiatives to improve quality outcomes, patient safety, and patient experience.

Ensure operational systems and processes support best practices in clinical care delivery and high reliability principles.

Maintain readiness for regulatory and accreditation requirements, including state and federal agencies and accrediting bodies.

Promote accountability for quality, safety, and service outcomes across all operational areas.

Technology and Digital Transformation Partner with executive leadership to implement and optimize enterprise systems, including electronic medical records and operational technologies.

Support digital transformation initiatives that enhance clinical workflows, data integration, operational efficiency, and patient access.

Leverage data analytics to inform decision-making and improve organizational performance.

Community, Academic, and External Engagement Work closely with university leadership to strengthen alignment between hospital operations and academic, teaching, and research programs.

Collaborate with external partners, community organizations, and civic leaders to improve healthcare access and care coordination.

Represent the hospital in operational partnerships, regional collaborations, and external engagements as appropriate.

Key Goals and Priorities The COO will focus on: Driving measurable improvements in operational performance, efficiency, and financial sustainability Strengthening patient access, throughput, and care coordination across the continuum of care Supporting large-scale facility modernization and enterprise operational transformation Enhancing clinical service line performance, growth, and integration Advancing a culture of accountability, collaboration, and operational excellence Supporting the CEO and executive leadership in achieving strategic, academic, and community-focused priorities Leadership Competencies Operational and Financial Excellence Demonstrated ability to lead complex healthcare operations while achieving improvements in efficiency, quality, and financial performance.

Strategic Execution Proven ability to translate organizational strategy into operational initiatives and measurable results across a large, complex enterprise.

Analytical andData-DrivenDecisionMaking Analytical and DataDriven Decision Making Leverages data, analytics, and performance metrics to guide decisionmaking and drive organizational performance.

Change Leadership Experience leading large-scale transformation initiatives, including operational, cultural, and infrastructure modernization.

Collaboration and Relationship Building Builds strong, effective partnerships with physicians, faculty, staff, executive leadership, and community stakeholders.

Communication and Executive Influence Demonstrates strong communication skills and the ability to influence and align multidisciplinary teams and stakeholders at all levels of the organization.

Commitment to Mission and Health Equity Demonstrated commitment to advancing health equity and serving diverse, underserved populations within a safety-net academic medical center environment.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Master’s Degree in Healthcare Administration, Business Administration, Public Health, or a related field required.
Minimum of 8 years of progressively responsible leadership experience in hospital or health system operations, including significant experience in a senior executive role (e.g., COO, Deputy COO, Senior Vice President of
Operations, or equivalent).
Demonstrated experience leading operations within a large, complex hospital or academic medical center, including oversight of inpatient, outpatient, and support services.
Proven track record of accountability for operational and financial performance, including improving efficiency, throughput, cost management, and overall organizational performance.
Experience leading large-scale operational transformation and performance improvement initiatives, including patient flow, length of stay, and access improvement.
Demonstrated ability to partner effectively with physician leadership, department chairs, and clinical teams in a highly matrixed environment.
Experience managing and developing large, multidisciplinary teams in a complex healthcare setting.

President & Chief Executive Officer 

Coalition Against Bigger Trucks (CABT) Washington, D.C.

Base Salary: Competitive, commensurate with experience - $250,000 - $300,000 base salary with room for bonus compensation. 

About CABT 

The Coalition Against Bigger Trucks (CABT) is a national coalition of law enforcement, first responders, safety advocates, labor organizations, trucking interests, railroads, suppliers, taxpayer and consumer organizations, and other stakeholders working to oppose increases in federal and state truck size and weight limits. 

For more than three decades, CABT has been a leading voice on truck size and weight policy. With a pending surface transportation reauthorization bill and renewed efforts to increase federal truck weight limits creating a consequential legislative environment, CABT’s new leadership will have an opportunity to build on the organization’s strong foundation and shape its next chapter as a more nimble, politically focused advocacy organization. 

CABT seeks a President & Chief Executive Officer
to lead this next chapter. 

The Opportunity 

The President & CEO will serve as CABT's chief executive and principal strategist. Based in Washington, D.C., the President will lead the coalition's federal advocacy strategy, congressional engagement, coalition management, organizational operations, and fundraising. 

This is first and foremost a senior government affairs and advocacy position. CABT seeks an experienced Washington leader who understands Congress and has demonstrated an ability to influence the legislative process as an outside advocate. 

Working closely with the Board of Directors and coalition partners, the President will lead an integrated approach combining direct lobbying, coalition advocacy, grassroots and grasstops mobilization, communications, and political intelligence. 

Key Responsibilities 

Advocacy & Strategy 

Serve as CABT's principal representative before Congress and the Administration. 
Develop and execute a bicameral bipartisan strategy to prevent increases in federal truck size and weight limits. 
Build and maintain strong relationships with Members of Congress, committee leadership, senior congressional staff, and other policymakers. 
Anticipate legislative threats and opportunities and develop proactive strategies around committee, floor, and conference action. 
Build and support a bipartisan network of congressional champions. 
Provide the Board and coalition partners with political intelligence, strategic recommendations, and assessments of the legislative environment. 
Coordinate with and support state-level partners responding to truck size and weight proposals, ensuring alignment with CABT’s broader federal advocacy strategy. 

Integrated Advocacy & Coalition Leadership 

Integrate government affairs, field organizing, grassroots, communications, research, and coalition engagement around a unified strategy. 
Mobilize coalition partners and influential constituents in priority states and congressional districts. 
Strengthen CABT's relationships with key validators, particularly law enforcement, first responders, highway safety advocates, state and local officials, labor, trucking, and transportation stakeholders. 
Recruit new organizations and voices that broaden CABT's political reach and credibility. 
Coordinate with communications and field partners to ensure outside advocacy reinforces CABT's direct lobbying efforts. 

Organizational Leadership & Fundraising 

Lead CABT's overall strategy, personnel, operations, budget, and organizational performance. 
Work closely with the Board of Directors to establish priorities and measure progress. 
Oversee staff, consultants, and outside partners. 
Maintain strong relationships with CABT's existing donors while broadening financial participation among coalition members and aligned organizations. 
Ensure CABT's resources are focused on activities that maximize political and advocacy impact. 

Candidate Qualifications 

The successful candidate will be an accomplished Washington government affairs professional with the experience, relationships, and political judgment to lead a sophisticated national advocacy organization. 

Candidates should have: 

10+ years of relevant professional experience in Congress, government affairs, public policy, political advocacy, or association leadership. 
Professional experience working on Capitol Hill, with a strong understanding of congressional procedure, committees, leadership, legislative strategy, and effective advocacy. 
A demonstrated record of personally engaging and lobbying Members of Congress and senior staff. 
Strong bipartisan and bicameral relationships and the ability to build new ones . 
Experience developing and executing strategies around consequential or politically challenging legislative issues. 
Demonstrated coalition-building and management skills. 
Experience managing staff, consultants, budgets, and outside partners. 
Strong political judgment and excellent written and verbal communication skills. 

Experience in transportation, infrastructure, highway safety, freight, trucking, or rail policy is beneficial but not required. Political sophistication, congressional experience, relationships, and a demonstrated record of effective advocacy are more important than prior subject-matter specialization. 

Leadership Profile 

CABT seeks a hands-on political strategist who understands how Washington actually works. The President should be comfortable personally engaging Members of Congress, counting votes, identifying champions and pressure points, and using coalition partners, constituents, communications, and grassroots advocacy to influence legislative outcomes. 

The successful candidate will also be a strong coalition builder and organizational leader capable of bringing diverse partners together around a common strategy and positioning CABT for long-term success. 

Compensation & Location 

CABT offers a competitive compensation package, with a base salary of up to $300,000, commensurate with experience and qualifications, along with benefits. 

The position is based in Washington, D.C., with a consistent in-person presence and regular engagement on Capitol Hill required.

Job Description

Program Director, Fidelity Charitable Catalyst Fund

Note: Fidelity will not provide immigration sponsorship for this position.

The Role

The Program Director for the Fidelity Charitable Catalyst Fund will lead the Fund’s state and local giving infrastructure work in the Deep South as well as its national grantmaking portfolio focused on donor engagement and education. This work aims to encourage individual donors to support promising nonprofits with limited access to philanthropic funding. This role requires experience engaging donors and nonprofits in the Deep South ( Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, Georgia, and South Carolina

Outstanding relationship-building and collaboration skills are necessary. A passion for strengthening nonprofit organizations is critical.

The Catalyst Fund team is led by an Executive Director who works closely with the Fidelity Charitable board of trustees and senior staff on strategy, impact assessment, finances, and external relations. The team represents Fidelity Charitable at many philanthropic and nonprofit convenings. The team also includes a Program Director responsible for managing our state and local strategy in the Southwest and Central Appalachia along with national grantees that elevate nonprofits and a Program Associate that supports the entire team and our grantees.

The Expertise And Skills You Bring

8 plus years of experience leading donor education/engagement/advising programs that connect individual donors with local nonprofits and/or nonprofit fundraising capacity building programs. Leadership and management experience at a community foundation, public foundation, giving circle, association of nonprofits, or similar community-based intermediary preferred.
undefined
4 plus years of experience as a grantmaker with responsibility for independently leading a portfolio (e.g., at the program officer or senior program officer level), assessing and recommending grants, managing ongoing grantee relationships, and conducting impact analysis on grants and across a portfolio.
undefined
Lived experience in the Deep South required, with demonstrated knowledge of philanthropy and the nonprofit sector across the region. Preference for candidates based in one of our current priority states, including Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, Georgia, or South Carolina.
Strong understanding of the latest national and local trends, research, and organizations influencing donor giving behavior, donor-advised funds, capacity building, and nonprofit fundraising; exceptional analytical, research, and writing skills; and significant public speaking experience with donor and nonprofit audiences.
Experience collaborating across diverse constituencies, building trust, achieving common goals, solving problems independently, taking initiative, and exercising sound judgment in fast-paced, ambiguous environments.
High proficiency with PowerPoint, Excel, and Word, along with experience using grants management systems (e.g., Fluxx).
Manage a portfolio of 40 plus grant relationships working in the Deep South and across the country, including community foundations, women’s foundations, giving platforms, giving circle networks, state associations of nonprofits, and other bridge builders. Develop relationships with potential grantees, complete grant diligence and assessments, make grant recommendations, and partner with grantees to set goals aligned with the Catalyst Fund's learning framework, monitor progress toward those goals, and analyze and synthesize grant reports.
Serve as a key representative of the Catalyst Fund across the Deep South and national donor support ecosystem, including speaking at grantee events, participating in funder conferences, and connecting national organizations to local grantees. Recommend revisions to the ongoing strategy and grantmaking priorities for local and national work by staying current on research, trends, and learning from grantees. Travel will be required for at least 50% of this role.

Fidelity Charitable is the leading donor-advised fund sponsor in the country with a simple mission—to grow the American tradition of philanthropy. We have helped donors support more than 461,000 nonprofit organizations with nearly $118 billion in grants. At Fidelity Charitable, our job is to help donors maximize their generosity by providing programs that make charitable giving accessible, simple, and effective.

The Catalyst Fund is a grantmaking program of Fidelity Charitable, led by its Board of Trustees and operating separately from Fidelity Charitable’s donor-advised fund program. The Fund provides grants to intermediary organizations that encourage donors to give more to promising nonprofits and help nonprofits strengthen their fundraising capacity, confidence, and ability to engage donors. The Fund is focused on growing resources for nonprofits in the Southwest, Deep South, and Central Appalachia, as well as organizations serving communities of color and rural communities nationwide. The Fund is organized across three portfolio areas—Engage Donors, Elevate Nonprofits, and Field Building—with funding divided between national grantees and state and local grantees.

Job Description

The Department of Hospital Administration at SUNY Downstate Health Sciences University is seeking a full-time Vice President & Chief Operating Officer.

Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer, the Chief Operating Officer (COO) of SUNY University Hospital at Downstate serves as a key member of the executive leadership team with enterprise-wide responsibility for hospital operations, operational performance, and care delivery systems.

The COO provides strategic and operational leadership across all clinical and support services, with accountability for the hospital’s day-to-day operations, quality and safety outcomes, workforce performance, and overall operational and financial performance in partnership with the Chief Financial Officer. This role ensures the delivery of high-quality, patient-centered care while advancing the hospital’s mission as Brooklyn’s only academic medical center and a critical safety-net provider serving diverse and underserved communities.

Working in close collaboration with the CEO and senior leadership of SUNY Downstate Health Sciences University, the COO plays a central role in executing the organization’s strategic priorities and driving enterprise performance. The COO leads large-scale operational transformation efforts, including improving patient access and throughput, advancing clinical service line performance, and supporting major capital and facility modernization initiatives. Strengthen integration across inpatient, outpatient, and community-based services to improve continuity of care and patient outcomes.

Ensure operational alignment with construction, regulatory, and transition timelines for capital projects and hospital expansion efforts.

Partner with Human Resources and clinical leadership on workforce planning, recruitment, retention, and leadership development strategies.

Promote collaboration and alignment among physicians, nurses, and multidisciplinary teams.

Support labor relations strategies and workforce engagement in a complex, unionized healthcare environment.

Ensure operational systems and processes support best practices in clinical care delivery and high reliability principles.

Maintain readiness for regulatory and accreditation requirements, including state and federal agencies and accrediting bodies.

Promote accountability for quality, safety, and service outcomes across all operational areas.

Support digital transformation initiatives that enhance clinical workflows, data integration, operational efficiency, and patient access.

Leverage data analytics to inform decision-making and improve organizational performance.

Collaborate with external partners, community organizations, and civic leaders to improve healthcare access and care coordination.

Represent the hospital in operational partnerships, regional collaborations, and external engagements as appropriate.

Communication and Executive Influence Demonstrates strong communication skills and the ability to influence and align multidisciplinary teams and stakeholders at all levels of the organization.

Master’s Degree in Healthcare Administration, Business Administration, Public Health, or a related field required.
Minimum of 8 years of progressively responsible leadership experience in hospital or health system operations, including significant experience in a senior executive role (e.g., COO, Deputy COO, Senior Vice President of
Operations, or equivalent).

new_jobs.description:
President & Chief Executive Officer 

Coalition Against Bigger Trucks (CABT) Washington, D.C.

Base Salary: Competitive, commensurate with experience - $250,000 - $300,000 base salary with room for bonus compensation. 

About CABT 

The Coalition Against Bigger Trucks (CABT) is a national coalition of law enforcement, first responders, safety advocates, labor organizations, trucking interests, railroads, suppliers, taxpayer and consumer organizations, and other stakeholders working to oppose increases in federal and state truck size and weight limits. 

For more than three decades, CABT has been a leading voice on truck size and weight policy. With a pending surface transportation reauthorization bill and renewed efforts to increase federal truck weight limits creating a consequential legislative environment, CABT’s new leadership will have an opportunity to build on the organization’s strong foundation and shape its next chapter as a more nimble, politically focused advocacy organization. 

CABT seeks a President & Chief Executive Officer
to lead this next chapter. 

The Opportunity 

The President & CEO will serve as CABT's chief executive and principal strategist. Based in Washington, D.C., the President will lead the coalition's federal advocacy strategy, congressional engagement, coalition management, organizational operations, and fundraising. 

This is first and foremost a senior government affairs and advocacy position. CABT seeks an experienced Washington leader who understands Congress and has demonstrated an ability to influence the legislative process as an outside advocate. 

Working closely with the Board of Directors and coalition partners, the President will lead an integrated approach combining direct lobbying, coalition advocacy, grassroots and grasstops mobilization, communications, and political intelligence. 

Key Responsibilities 

Advocacy & Strategy 

Serve as CABT's principal representative before Congress and the Administration. 
Develop and execute a bicameral bipartisan strategy to prevent increases in federal truck size and weight limits. 
Build and maintain strong relationships with Members of Congress, committee leadership, senior congressional staff, and other policymakers. 
Anticipate legislative threats and opportunities and develop proactive strategies around committee, floor, and conference action. 
Build and support a bipartisan network of congressional champions. 
Provide the Board and coalition partners with political intelligence, strategic recommendations, and assessments of the legislative environment. 
Coordinate with and support state-level partners responding to truck size and weight proposals, ensuring alignment with CABT’s broader federal advocacy strategy. 

Integrated Advocacy & Coalition Leadership 

Integrate government affairs, field organizing, grassroots, communications, research, and coalition engagement around a unified strategy. 
Mobilize coalition partners and influential constituents in priority states and congressional districts. 
Strengthen CABT's relationships with key validators, particularly law enforcement, first responders, highway safety advocates, state and local officials, labor, trucking, and transportation stakeholders. 
Recruit new organizations and voices that broaden CABT's political reach and credibility. 
Coordinate with communications and field partners to ensure outside advocacy reinforces CABT's direct lobbying efforts. 

Organizational Leadership & Fundraising 

Lead CABT's overall strategy, personnel, operations, budget, and organizational performance. 
Work closely with the Board of Directors to establish priorities and measure progress. 
Oversee staff, consultants, and outside partners. 
Maintain strong relationships with CABT's existing donors while broadening financial participation among coalition members and aligned organizations. 
Ensure CABT's resources are focused on activities that maximize political and advocacy impact. 

Candidate Qualifications 

The successful candidate will be an accomplished Washington government affairs professional with the experience, relationships, and political judgment to lead a sophisticated national advocacy organization. 

Candidates should have: 

10+ years of relevant professional experience in Congress, government affairs, public policy, political advocacy, or association leadership. 
Professional experience working on Capitol Hill, with a strong understanding of congressional procedure, committees, leadership, legislative strategy, and effective advocacy. 
A demonstrated record of personally engaging and lobbying Members of Congress and senior staff. 
Strong bipartisan and bicameral relationships and the ability to build new ones . 
Experience developing and executing strategies around consequential or politically challenging legislative issues. 
Demonstrated coalition-building and management skills. 
Experience managing staff, consultants, budgets, and outside partners. 
Strong political judgment and excellent written and verbal communication skills. 

Experience in transportation, infrastructure, highway safety, freight, trucking, or rail policy is beneficial but not required. Political sophistication, congressional experience, relationships, and a demonstrated record of effective advocacy are more important than prior subject-matter specialization. 

Leadership Profile 

CABT seeks a hands-on political strategist who understands how Washington actually works. The President should be comfortable personally engaging Members of Congress, counting votes, identifying champions and pressure points, and using coalition partners, constituents, communications, and grassroots advocacy to influence legislative outcomes. 

The successful candidate will also be a strong coalition builder and organizational leader capable of bringing diverse partners together around a common strategy and positioning CABT for long-term success. 

Compensation & Location 

CABT offers a competitive compensation package, with a base salary of up to $300,000, commensurate with experience and qualifications, along with benefits. 

The position is based in Washington, D.C., with a consistent in-person presence and regular engagement on Capitol Hill required. 

Interested candidates should submit a resume and cover letter to cabtexecutivesearch@gmail.com .

new_jobs.description:
Director of Fund Development

Salary Commensurate with Experience
Expected Range: $90,000 - $125,000

Position Summary

Beat the Streets National seeks an experienced Director of Fund Development to lead and
execute the organization’s fundraising efforts in partnership with the Executive Director and
Fund Development Committee.

This is a hands-on fundraising role for an experienced development professional who can both
build strategy and execute it. The Director will manage a portfolio of donors and prospects,
cultivate and solicit major gifts, strengthen donor stewardship and renewal systems, lead
fundraising campaigns, and create the development infrastructure necessary to support Beat
the Streets National’s continued growth.

The Executive Director will remain actively involved in major donor relationships, principal gifts,
and overall fundraising strategy. The Director will work closely with the Executive Director to
identify opportunities, manage donor strategy and follow-through, and increasingly expand the
organization’s fundraising capacity beyond relationships managed directly by the Executive
Director.

This position currently has no direct reports. The successful candidate must be comfortable
operating as both a senior fundraising strategist and an individual contributor, personally
managing donor relationships while also handling the writing, research, tracking, coordination,
and development operations necessary to move opportunities forward.
Key Responsibilities

Major Gifts and Donor Development

● Manage a portfolio of individual donors and prospects, including qualification, cultivation,
solicitation, renewal, and stewardship.
● Personally solicit major gifts and develop strategies for increasing donor engagement
and giving.
● Partner with the Executive Director on high-level donor relationships, including prospect
strategy, meeting preparation, solicitation planning, and follow-up.
● Identify opportunities to move existing supporters into deeper and longer-term
relationships with Beat the Streets National.
● Develop individualized cultivation and stewardship plans for priority donors and
prospects.
● Build a disciplined pipeline of prospective individual, corporate, and foundation
supporters.
● Ensure consistent and timely donor follow-up, acknowledgment, stewardship, pledge
collection, and renewal activity.
Fundraising Strategy and Execution
● Work with the Executive Director and Fund Development Committee to develop and
execute an annual fund development strategy.
● Establish fundraising goals, priorities, timelines, and measurable activity targets.
● Develop a balanced fundraising approach across major gifts, annual giving, corporate
partnerships, foundations, sponsorships, and campaign-based giving.
● Build and maintain a development calendar that coordinates solicitations, renewals,
campaigns, events, grant opportunities, and stewardship activity.
● Regularly evaluate fundraising performance and recommend adjustments based on
results and pipeline development.
Campaigns and Sponsorships
● Lead fundraising execution for national initiatives including GearUp!, National Camp &
Duals, Celebration of Impact, and other Beat the Streets National priorities.
● Develop campaign strategies, donor segmentation, solicitation materials, sponsorship
opportunities, and stewardship plans.
● Identify and cultivate corporate partners whose philanthropic and business interests
align with Beat the Streets National.
● Manage sponsorship outreach, commitments, fulfillment, recognition, and renewal
opportunities.
● Coordinate donor engagement surrounding national events and other strategic
opportunities.
Development Operations
● Maintain accurate donor records, gift histories, prospect information, pledges,
communications, and next steps within the organization’s CRM.
● Establish consistent systems for moves management, donor tracking, forecasting, and
follow-up.
● Prepare fundraising dashboards, pipeline reports, revenue projections, and development
updates for the Executive Director, Fund Development Committee, and Board.
● Track deadlines for grants, reports, renewals, campaigns, sponsorships, and donor
commitments.
● Maintain high standards for data integrity and development documentation.
● Coordinate gift acknowledgments, pledge reminders, donor recognition, and other core
development processes.
Prospect Research and Fundraising Communications
● Conduct prospect research on individuals, foundations, corporations, and strategic
partners.
● Prepare donor briefings and recommended engagement strategies for priority prospects.
● Draft compelling donor communications, proposals, sponsorship materials, grant
requests, cases for support, impact updates, and stewardship materials.
● Translate Beat the Streets National’s mission, programs, outcomes, and growth strategy
into clear and persuasive fundraising messages.
● Work with program and leadership teams to collect impact stories, outcomes, photos,
and other materials that strengthen donor engagement.
Board and Fund Development Committee Engagement
● Serve as the primary staff partner, alongside the Executive Director, to the Fund
Development Committee.
● Prepare fundraising reports, pipeline updates, prospect discussions, and recommended
action items for committee meetings.
● Help Board and committee members identify, cultivate, and engage potential supporters.
● Provide Board members with clear outreach strategies, donor information, talking points,
and follow-up support.
● Build greater consistency and accountability around Board participation in fundraising.
Qualifications
● Approximately 5 to 8+ years of progressive nonprofit fundraising or closely related
development experience.
● Demonstrated experience cultivating, soliciting, and closing major gifts from individual
donors.
● Strong understanding of donor cultivation, moves management, stewardship, renewals,
and relationship-based fundraising.
● Experience managing a portfolio of donors and prospects with measurable fundraising
responsibility.
● Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to develop
persuasive donor correspondence and proposals.
● Excellent organization, judgment, attention to detail, and follow-through.
● Ability to manage multiple priorities independently in a growing and entrepreneurial
organization.
● Experience working directly with executive leadership, Board members, volunteers, and
sophisticated donors.
● Experience with CRM or donor management systems and comfort using data to manage
fundraising activity and performance.
● Corporate fundraising, foundation relations, sponsorship, campaign, or event fundraising
experience is strongly preferred.
● Passion for youth development, sports-based youth development, education, mentoring,
wrestling, or community impact is strongly valued.

Ideal Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate is an experienced fundraiser who combines strong relationship-building
skills with disciplined execution.

They are comfortable sitting across the table from a significant donor and making an appropriate
solicitation, but equally willing to prepare the meeting brief, update the CRM, draft the follow-up
email, and ensure the next step happens on time.

They understand that Beat the Streets National is a growing organization and that this role
requires both leadership and execution. Rather than inheriting a large development department,
this individual will help build the fundraising systems, donor pipeline, and culture necessary to
support the organization’s next stage of growth.

The successful candidate will be confident enough to operate independently while recognizing
that fundraising at Beat the Streets National is highly collaborative. They will work closely with
the Executive Director, Board, Fund Development Committee, and national network to deepen
existing relationships and develop new sources of philanthropic support.

Measures of Success

Success in this role will include:
● Growth in contributed revenue and the major gift pipeline.
● Successful cultivation, solicitation, and closure of new and renewed major gifts.
● Increased donor retention, renewal, and upgrading.
● Expansion of donor relationships beyond those managed exclusively by the Executive
Director.
● A more disciplined and consistently managed prospect pipeline.
● Improved forecasting, donor tracking, stewardship, and follow-through.
● Stronger execution of national fundraising campaigns and sponsorship efforts.
● Increased engagement of Board and Fund Development Committee members in
fundraising.
● Development of sustainable fundraising systems that position Beat the Streets National
for continued growth.

At The Obama Foundation, our mission is to inspire, empower, and connect people to change their world. We seek to build an active democratic culture where people are equipped and motivated to make change in the communities where they live, work, and play. Right here on the South Side of Chicago, we’re building a home for this vision, a global center for change with a range of opportunities - coordinated programming, community outreach events, educational moments, and more - that invite visitors from down the block or across the globe to turn hope into action.

Achieving our ambitious goals starts with an exceptional team built on our Hope to Action Values - Courage, Empathy, Integrity, Accountability, Community, Inclusivity, Pragmatism, Resilience, Imagination, and Hope. A Framework that anyone, anywhere, can use to build trust, activate participation, and expand opportunity in their community.

Purpose of the Role

The Chief of Staff (COS), Office of the Executive Vice President (EVP) of Programs will partner with the EVP of Programs as a strategic and administrative operator to ensure the EVP’s time and attention are aligned with the objectives of the Foundation’s Programs department. The EVP of Programs is a member of the Foundation’s Executive Leadership Team and is a highly visible principal whose role is cross functional and collaborative with Executive Office & Strategy, People, Legal, Finance, Development, OPC, and External Affairs partners.

The COS will work closely with the Vice President of Program Operations to help drive operational excellence for the Programs department. This position serves as a critical member of the Program Operations Leadership table, managed by the Vice President of Program Operations.

Core Job Responsibilities

EVP project management & decision making: Maintain the submission form and tracker of all memos and materials requiring the EVP’s awareness, feedback, and / or decision making. Proactively communicate with all stakeholders the protocols for engaging with the EVP, and work closely with the Vice President of Operations to respond to incoming inquiries pertaining to the full Programs department. Serve as a strategic thought-partner to the EVP to support decision-making and improve operating culture, and serve as the EVP’s proxy when not present.
Scheduling and meeting support: Ensure that the EVP is fully prepared for all meetings with agendas, bios, talking points, briefings and background reading. This includes preparing meeting materials such as agendas, memos, and presentations, as well as tracking and communicating meeting takeaways and next steps. When appropriate, staff the EVP in meetings to document and track next steps. Facilitate the weekly Programs Leadership Team meeting. Design and improve processes and systems for communication and cross-team collaboration.
Manage external speaking requests: Organize and prioritize all external speaking requests for the EVP in collaboration with the Foundation’s Marketing and Communications team. Manage Support Services: Regularly convene and advise all Program staff who provide administrative support to other Program Vice Presidents and consultants (as needed). Work collaboratively to manage a range of responsibilities: managing EVP consultant contracts and invoices, processing Program stakeholder requests for tickets and access to the Obama Presidential Center; and tracking and responding to inquiries interested in Foundation programs and partnership.
Data Input: Ensure that all external communication (via email, phone call, or meetings) are entered into the appropriate data management system in a timely manner.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Key Deliverables / Outcomes

Act as a trusted extension of the EVP - anticipating needs, provide exceptional customer service, and show up as a credible proxy
Trust, respect, and discretion with a range of internal and external stakeholders, including high-profile principals
EVP’s calendar is up-to-date and reflective of work priorities

Timely and responsive administrative support for Programs department staff
Clear, timely, and intentional team communications and meetings, on behalf of the EVP
Meeting requests are replied to within 1 business day
Travel arrangements for the EVP are made on-time and within budget

Required Qualifications

A minimum of 5 years of work experience in executive administration or operations; nonprofit or government industry experience preferred but not required.
Strategic judgment – works to understand the Foundation’s culture and priorities and can connect short-term execution to long-term goals; exercises sound judgment in situations with multiple, complex considerations and stakeholder interests
Project Management experience – effectively plan and execute short- and long-term projects; track record of designing and implementing effective and efficient systems and processes that deliver excellent results

Strong prioritization and organizational skills to effectively juggle short-term and long-term tasks and responsibilities in an entrepreneurial, fast-paced environment
Motivated by exceptional customer service; anticipates needs, takes initiative, resourceful, problem-solver

Job Description

Program Director, Fidelity Charitable Catalyst Fund

Note: Fidelity will not provide immigration sponsorship for this position.

The Role

The Program Director for the Fidelity Charitable Catalyst Fund will lead the Fund’s state and local giving infrastructure work in the Deep South as well as its national grantmaking portfolio focused on donor engagement and education. This work aims to encourage individual donors to support promising nonprofits with limited access to philanthropic funding. This role requires experience engaging donors and nonprofits in the Deep South ( Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, Georgia, and South Carolina
) and independently managing a grant portfolio. Candidates need deep knowledge of the philanthropy ecosystem, particularly in the South, and ideally, donor-advised funds and high-net wealthy donors. Outstanding relationship-building and collaboration skills are necessary. A passion for strengthening nonprofit organizations is critical.

The Catalyst Fund team is led by an Executive Director who works closely with the Fidelity Charitable board of trustees and senior staff on strategy, impact assessment, finances, and external relations. The team represents Fidelity Charitable at many philanthropic and nonprofit convenings. The team also includes a Program Director responsible for managing our state and local strategy in the Southwest and Central Appalachia along with national grantees that elevate nonprofits and a Program Associate that supports the entire team and our grantees.

The Expertise And Skills You Bring

8 plus years of experience leading donor education/engagement/advising programs that connect individual donors with local nonprofits and/or nonprofit fundraising capacity building programs. Leadership and management experience at a community foundation, public foundation, giving circle, association of nonprofits, or similar community-based intermediary preferred.
undefined
4 plus years of experience as a grantmaker with responsibility for independently leading a portfolio (e.g., at the program officer or senior program officer level), assessing and recommending grants, managing ongoing grantee relationships, and conducting impact analysis on grants and across a portfolio.
undefined
Lived experience in the Deep South required, with demonstrated knowledge of philanthropy and the nonprofit sector across the region. Preference for candidates based in one of our current priority states, including Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Alabama, Georgia, or South Carolina.
Strong understanding of the latest national and local trends, research, and organizations influencing donor giving behavior, donor-advised funds, capacity building, and nonprofit fundraising; exceptional analytical, research, and writing skills; and significant public speaking experience with donor and nonprofit audiences.
Experience collaborating across diverse constituencies, building trust, achieving common goals, solving problems independently, taking initiative, and exercising sound judgment in fast-paced, ambiguous environments.
High proficiency with PowerPoint, Excel, and Word, along with experience using grants management systems (e.g., Fluxx).
Manage a portfolio of 40 plus grant relationships working in the Deep South and across the country, including community foundations, women’s foundations, giving platforms, giving circle networks, state associations of nonprofits, and other bridge builders. Develop relationships with potential grantees, complete grant diligence and assessments, make grant recommendations, and partner with grantees to set goals aligned with the Catalyst Fund's learning framework, monitor progress toward those goals, and analyze and synthesize grant reports.
Serve as a key representative of the Catalyst Fund across the Deep South and national donor support ecosystem, including speaking at grantee events, participating in funder conferences, and connecting national organizations to local grantees. Recommend revisions to the ongoing strategy and grantmaking priorities for local and national work by staying current on research, trends, and learning from grantees. Travel will be required for at least 50% of this role.
Partner with the Executive Director on grantee learning events and communications, process improvements, board communications, and special projects.
Partner across Fidelity Charitable teams to launch experiments that encourage donors to give directly to, or in alignment with, the Catalyst Fund.
Partner with Fidelity Charitable's Marketing team to promote the work of local and national grantees and inspire Fidelity Charitable donor engagement with grantees.

The Team

Fidelity Charitable is the leading donor-advised fund sponsor in the country with a simple mission—to grow the American tradition of philanthropy. We have helped donors support more than 461,000 nonprofit organizations with nearly $118 billion in grants. At Fidelity Charitable, our job is to help donors maximize their generosity by providing programs that make charitable giving accessible, simple, and effective.

Company Overview

The Catalyst Fund is a grantmaking program of Fidelity Charitable, led by its Board of Trustees and operating separately from Fidelity Charitable’s donor-advised fund program. The Fund provides grants to intermediary organizations that encourage donors to give more to promising nonprofits and help nonprofits strengthen their fundraising capacity, confidence, and ability to engage donors. The Fund is focused on growing resources for nonprofits in the Southwest, Deep South, and Central Appalachia, as well as organizations serving communities of color and rural communities nationwide. The Fund is organized across three portfolio areas—Engage Donors, Elevate Nonprofits, and Field Building—with funding divided between national grantees and state and local grantees.

Join the Oregon Symphony Team as our Director of Development, Planned and Major Gifts!

As our Director of Development, Planned and Major Gifts, you will help shape the future of the Oregon Symphony by building meaningful relationships with donors whose generosity sustains our mission for generations to come. Through strategic major gift fundraising, planned giving, and thoughtful donor stewardship, you'll play a key role in advancing philanthropic support and strengthening the Symphony's long-term financial future.

Here's how you'll make a difference:
Build and manage a portfolio of major and planned giving donors and prospects, developing meaningful relationships that inspire transformational philanthropy.
Develop and execute individualized cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies that align donor passions with the Symphony's mission.
Lead the Oregon Symphony's planned giving program, expanding legacy giving opportunities and encouraging long-term philanthropic investment.
Prepare compelling major, blended, and planned gift proposals that help donors achieve their charitable goals while advancing organizational priorities.
Partner with the Vice President of Development, Board members, and fellow fundraisers to cultivate and solicit high-capacity donors.
Mentor Development team members on planned giving strategies and emerging gift opportunities, strengthening fundraising capacity across the department.
Create planned giving materials and donor communications that clearly communicate the impact of philanthropy.
Represent the Symphony at donor meetings, concerts, cultivation events, and community gatherings, building lasting relationships with supporters.
Monitor portfolio performance, donor activity, and fundraising progress to help achieve annual and long-term revenue goals.

This role is pivotal in helping ensure the Oregon Symphony's artistic excellence continues to flourish for generations to come. If you're passionate about building lasting donor relationships and creating meaningful philanthropic partnerships, we'd love to have you on the team.

Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree and at least five years of fundraising experience with a focus on major and planned gifts, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

•       Support data integrity and reporting used for client reviews, payroll / benefits, and internal decision-making
